title: Over a henselian pair, $V(\mathfrak p+I)$ is connected
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $\mathfrak p\subseteq A$ a prime ideal. Then the closed subset $V(\mathfrak p+I)=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A:\mathfrak q\supseteq\mathfrak p+I\}$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] in the subspace topology (in particular nonempty).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.16 (Tag 09Y6, label lemma-irreducible-henselian-pair-connected, line 2948); 'connected' includes nonempty (Topology, Definition 5.7.1)

proof.text: *Step 1 (reduce to a domain).* The quotient map $A\to A/\mathfrak p$ is integral, and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair] therefore makes $(A/\mathfrak p,(I+\mathfrak p)/\mathfrak p)$ a henselian pair. Since $\mathfrak p$ is prime, $A/\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero domain. The quotient-spectrum description identifies $\operatorname{Spec}((A/\mathfrak p)/((I+\mathfrak p)/\mathfrak p))$ homeomorphically with the subspace $V(\mathfrak p+I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$: the map for a quotient is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], and its image consists exactly of primes containing the quotient ideal by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus it is enough to prove that if $(A,I)$ is henselian and $A$ is a nonzero domain, then $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is connected.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.16 (Tag 09Y6), proof: first paragraph, using Lemma 15.11.8 (Tag 09XK)

proof.text: *Step 2 (the quotient is nonzero).* The quotient $A/I$ cannot be the zero ring. Otherwise, applying the henselian lifting condition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] to the finite $A$-algebra $B=A$, the unique idempotent of $B/IB=0$ would have the two distinct lifts $0$ and $1$ in the nonzero domain $A$, contradicting uniqueness. Hence the hypothesis needed for the affine connectedness criterion applies to $A/I$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.16 (Tag 09Y6), proof together with the nonzero-ring hypothesis of Algebra, Lemma 10.21.2 (Tag 00E9)

proof.text: *Step 3 (idempotent contradiction).* If $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ were disconnected, the affine clopen-idempotent correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] would give a nontrivial idempotent $\bar e\in A/I$: choose a nonempty proper clopen piece of the disconnection, and its corresponding idempotent is neither $0$ nor $1$. Apply the henselian condition to $B=A$ to lift $\bar e$ to an idempotent $e\in A$. Since $A$ is a domain, $e(e-1)=0$ forces $e=0$ or $e=1$, whose reductions are respectively $0$ or $1$, contrary to the choice of $\bar e$. Therefore $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is connected, and Step 1 transports this connectedness (including nonemptiness) to $V(\mathfrak p+I)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.16 (Tag 09Y6), proof: second paragraph, using Algebra, Lemma 10.21.2 (Tag 00E9) and the characterization of henselian pairs in Lemma 15.11.6 (Tag 09XI)

The quotient-spectrum homeomorphism is made explicit using the existing quotient closed-immersion Mathlib leaf and affine-spectrum definition; the affine clopen-idempotent correspondence supplies the contradiction. No new nodes were needed, and the item already had the required three Mathlib searches.
